text:
sarah: Observed a perf regression on canary after driver bump to 544.23 — seq=512 P95 up ~12% and throughput drop on tensor-core kernels.
ops-bot: canary-deploy: deployment r-2026-03-18 applied to batch-5 (5% traffic)
jordan: Can you paste a repro and perf snippet?
sarah: Repro run against canary endpoint:
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood-inference/models/gpt-xl/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY' \
  -d '{"prompt":"x","max_new_tokens":512,"batch_size":1}'
```
Perf sample from the canary host (nvprof-like summary):
```
seq=512 batch=1 kernel=masked_attn_fwd_v2 selected
avg p99 latency: 216ms (baseline 193ms)
throughput tok/s: 4.2k (baseline 4.8k)
```
mike: autotuner is picking masked_attn_fwd_v2 now, previously v1. v2 uses tensor cores with different tiling heuristics — looks like driver math precision changed cost model.
anya: Quick mitigation options: 1) autotuner blacklist for v2 on A100/driver 544.23 2) force fallback to v1 for seq<=1024 3) rollback driver on canary hosts
jordan: Ran a profiler, kernel cost distribution shows higher warp-stall on v2 for short sequences:
```
kernel masked_attn_fwd_v2: warp_stall 28% cycles, memory_l1_miss 1.6%
kernel masked_attn_fwd_v1: warp_stall 8% cycles, memory_l1_miss 0.9%
```
sarah: Given canary impact, propose: apply autotuner heuristic patch (prefer v1 if seq <= 768) as immediate hotfix, plus rollback driver on canary until patch lands. I'll open PR and patch canary config.
mike: I'll prepare a rollback runbook and start driver rollback on 2/5 canary hosts, ops-bot will report.
ops-bot: rollback-started: hosts batch-5 node-03 node-07
anya: Also capturing KV-cache reuse profile — we'll check if K/V cache fragmentation correlates.
sarah: Filed RFC + tracking issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4921
jordan: OK let's meet 20m to sync after initial rollback numbers
mike: :thumbsup:
